{{nihongo|'''Hamana Sōsha-shinmeigū'''|濱名惣社神明宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tōtōmi Province]].

===History===
Its founding details are unclear, but oral tradition says that {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}}, daughter of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, carrying the {{ill|Imperial Regalia of Japan|Q327465|qid=Q327465}} by divine command of {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Sume-Ōmikami}}, came by ship to this area guided by {{ill|Ōta-no-Mikoto|Q97496337|qid=Q97496337}}, after passing through {{ill|Yamato|Q13417196|qid=Q13417196}}, {{ill|Iga|Q11380622|qid=Q11380622}}, {{ill|Ise|Q297053|qid=Q297053}}, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156|lt=Mino}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Owari}} in search of an enshrinement site, stayed for over forty days in a temporary palace, and then moved by further divine oracle to the side of the {{ill|Isuzu River|Q6089522|qid=Q6089522}} in Watarai, Ise.

The honden is said to have been used as a storage building for tribute goods sent from Hamana Kanbe to {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|abstract|Q687168|ar|ضريح إيسه|ca|Santuari d'Ise|cs|Svatyně Ise|de|Ise-jingū|el|Μεγάλο Ιερό της Ίσε|eo|Ise-Sanktejo|es|Santuario de Ise|eu|Ise santutegi handia|fa|معبد ایسه|fi|Ise-jingū|fr|Sanctuaire d'Ise|he|מקדש איסה|hu|Iszei nagyszentély|id|Kuil Besar Ise|it|Santuario di Ise|ja|伊勢神宮|ka|ისე-ძინგუ|ko|이세 신궁|ky|Исе ибадатканасы|la|Ise Magnum Templum|lfn|Santeria de Ise|lv|Ises svētnīca|min|Kuil Gadang Ise|ml|ഐസ് ഗ്രാൻഡ് ക്ഷേത്രം|nl|Ise Jingu|no|Ise Jingū|or|ଇଶେ ମହାଶାଳ|pl|Ise-jingū|pt|Santuário de Ise|ru|Храм Исэ|sh|Veliko svetište Ise|simple|Ise Grand Shrine|sl|Veliko svetišče Ise|sv|Ise Jingū|th|ศาลเจ้าอิเซะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Ise|tr|Ise Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ісе|vi|Thần cung Ise|zh|伊势神宫|zh_min_nan|Ise Sîn-kiong|qid=Q687168}}. It is in Itakura-zukuri (Ikago-zukuri), a rare old-style form nationwide. It was deeply revered by successive {{ill|jiangjun|Q15903946|qid=Q15903946}} and provincial governors; in particular, shoguns of both the {{ill|Toyotomi clan|Q1521658|qid=Q1521658|lt=Toyotomi}} and {{ill|Tokugawa clan|Q1412769|qid=Q1412769|lt=Tokugawa}} are said to have set regulations and donated 42 koku of registered rice fields in reverence<ref>[https://genbu.net/data/toutoumi/sinmei_title.htm Hamana Sōsha-shinmeigū]</ref><ref>[http://www.shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4415060 Hamana Sōsha-shinmeigū - Shizuoka Shrine Office]</ref>.

It is treated as a candidate shrine for Eita Shrine of the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} list<ref name="Blog">Hisao Hoga, "[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/kaikokuso/kaikok2.htm Genealogy of the Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko and continuation of the clan]," 'Kojuki no Bōkan,' 2016.</ref>.

It was ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} on August 2, {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5.

On February 11, Meiji 40, it was designated for offerings of {{ill|Shinsen|Q11591045|qid=Q11591045}} and {{ill|Hanpei|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885}}.
===Enshrined deity===
*{{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Sume-Ōmikami}}
According to a precinct noticeboard, the {{ill|list of agatanushi|Q11582624|qid=Q11582624}} who ruled the Mikkabi area in ancient times enshrined their ancestral deity Ōta-no-Mikoto<ref name="Blog"/>, and when Mikkabi became Ise shrine land in {{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} 3 ({{ill|940|Q23830|qid=Q23830}}), Amaterasu Sume-Ōmikami became principal and Ōta-no-Mikoto moved to a subordinate position.
